skill.name: requirement-translator
skill.description: Converts vague or subjective product requests into structured, testable AI execution specifications. It identifies missing information, assumptions, constraints, acceptance criteria, risks, and implementation order.
skill.summary: Translate unclear requests into structured requirements that AI agents can execute.
skill.author: Barry-Liu-888

content.user_title: Translate Vague Requests Into Clear Specs
content.value_statement: Vague requests create missed details, weak acceptance criteria, and unclear execution. This skill turns them into structured specifications with assumptions, constraints, priorities, and next steps.
actual_capabilities: Extracts goals, ambiguous phrases, missing details, and implicit assumptions from a request.
Rewrites requests into goals, functional requirements, constraints, acceptance criteria, edge cases, and priorities.
Adds a recommended approach, risk notes, and implementation order after the translated specification.
Marks inferred content so users can review and correct assumptions.
Lists clarification questions when key details cannot be reasonably inferred.
Produces Chinese requirement specifications according to the skill instructions.
limitations: It does not validate business strategy, pricing, or market demand.
It cannot guarantee technical feasibility without project context and constraints.
It relies on user-provided context and may need follow-up questions.
It is designed to output Chinese specifications unless adapted by the user.

use_cases.title: Clarify Early Feature Ideas
use_cases.description: Turn rough stakeholder input into a structured requirement draft with goals, scope, and acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Prepare AI Coding Tasks
use_cases.description: Convert a broad implementation request into precise instructions that Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can follow.

use_cases.title: Align Design And Scope
use_cases.description: Separate visual intent, interaction needs, constraints, and open questions before design or development starts.

prompt_templates.title: Translate A Simple Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Translate this vague request into a structured requirement specification: [paste request]. Include goals, functional needs, constraints, and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Find Missing Details
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this requirement for ambiguity and missing information: [paste request]. List assumptions, inferred details, and questions that need user confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Create An Execution Spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this product request into an implementation-ready specification: [paste request]. Include priorities, edge cases, risks, and a recommended build order.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Possible Interpretations
prompt_templates.prompt: This request can be interpreted in multiple ways: [paste request]. Compare the interpretations, choose the safest default, and produce a final structured specification.

output: Goal: Improve the dashboard so users can find priority metrics faster.
Functional needs: clarify key metrics, add filtering, and improve empty states.
Acceptance criteria: users can identify the top metrics within one screen.
Questions: Which metrics matter most, and who uses the dashboard?

output_examples.input: Build a good signup page for our app.
output: Goal: Create a signup flow that helps new users create accounts with minimal friction.
Design constraints: use clear labels, visible validation, and mobile-friendly layout.
Edge cases: duplicate email, weak password, network failure, and empty fields.
Priority: account creation, validation, error handling, then optional social login.

output_examples.input: Optimize search so it feels faster.
output: Goal: Reduce perceived search latency and improve result clarity.
Inferred requirement: show loading feedback when results take more than one second.
Acceptance criteria: results appear or a useful status appears within one second.
Risks: actual backend latency may still need separate measurement and tuning.

best_practices: Provide the original request, intended users, platform, and known constraints.
Review every marked assumption before using the specification for implementation.
Add measurable acceptance criteria after the first translation.
anti_patterns: Do not treat inferred details as approved decisions.
Do not use the output as a final contract without stakeholder review.
Do not ask for broad improvement without naming the target user or success metric.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It turns vague requirements into structured specifications with goals, constraints, acceptance criteria, risks, and next steps.

faq.question: Can it ask clarification questions?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists questions when key details are missing and cannot be reasonably inferred.

faq.question: Does it replace a product manager?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure requirements, but stakeholders must still approve decisions and priorities.

faq.question: Can developers use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It can prepare clearer implementation instructions for Codex, Claude, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What language does it use?
faq.answer: The source skill instructs the assistant to output Chinese requirement specifications.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: Give the raw request, target users, platform, constraints, and any known success measures.
